elements.reason: The abstract text (text_2) does not explicitly state that the report is a 'systematic review', although the document title indicates this.

elements.quote: The aim of this study was to investigate the effects of the use of Point-of-Care Ultrasound (PoCUS) versus conventional management on clinical outcomes in patients with acute onset dyspnea.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states the aim/objective of the study.

elements.quote: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs), and prospective and retrospective cohort studies that compared PoCUS with conventional diagnostic modalities (controls) in patients with acute onset dyspnea were included.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies inclusion criteria but does not explicitly list exclusion criteria.

elements.quote: The Cochrane Library, MEDLINE, EMBASE and reference lists were searched to identify eligible trials (inception to October 14, 2021).
elements.reason: The abstract identifies the information sources and the date the search was last conducted.

elements.quote: Two independent reviewers extracted data and assessed the risk of bias.
elements.reason: The abstract mentions risk of bias assessment but does not specify the method or tool used (e.g., Cochrane RoB 2).
The abstract does not specify the methods used to present and synthesize the results (e.g., meta-analysis model).

elements.quote: We included eight RCTs and six observational studies with a total of 5393 participants.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies and participants.

elements.quote: Time to diagnosis (mean difference [MD], - 63 min; 95% CI, - 115 to - 11 min] and time to treatment (MD, - 27 min; 95% CI - 43 to - 11 min) were significantly shorter in the PoCUS group.
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcomes with effect sizes and confidence intervals.

elements.quote: Time to diagnosis (mean difference [MD], - 63 min; 95% CI, - 115 to - 11 min]...
elements.reason: A meta-analysis was conducted and the abstract reports summary estimates and confidence intervals.

elements.quote: ...significantly shorter in the PoCUS group.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates the direction of effect and that the PoCUS group was favored.

elements.quote: Heterogeneity across studies was variable (from low to considerable), with overall low or moderate study quality and low or moderate risk of bias (except one article with serious risk of bias).
elements.reason: The abstract summarizes limitations regarding heterogeneity and risk of bias.

elements.quote: Our results indicate that PoCUS use contributes to early diagnosis and better outcomes compared to conventional methods in patients admitted with acute onset dyspnea.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and their implications.
The abstract text does not specify the primary source of funding for the review.
The abstract text does not provide the register name and registration number.

elements.quote: There is an increasing body of evidence demonstrating that the accuracy of PoCUS is comparable to the current imaging reference standard CXR in general... However, very few trials have examined meaningful clinical outcomes related to PoCUS usage to date [23] and the results on outcome measurements were heterogeneous [24].
elements.reason: Describes the current state of knowledge (accuracy comparable to CXR) and important uncertainties (few trials on clinical outcomes, heterogeneous results).

elements.quote: Acute-onset dyspnea is one of the most common symptoms... 30-day mortality rate of these patients remains relatively high... Therefore, rapid and appropriate diagnosis of the underlying pathology is of utmost importance... Therefore, we conducted a high-quality, comprehensive systematic review...
elements.reason: Explains the importance (high mortality, common symptom) and need for the review (rapid diagnosis important, conventional methods have doubts).

elements.quote: In addition to the existing diagnostic accuracy studies [16-20, 25], our main objective, as a new insight to this field, was to investigate how PoCUS improves clinical endpoints in patients with acute onset dyspnea.
elements.reason: Identifies previous reviews (diagnostic accuracy studies) and explains the need for the current review (investigating clinical endpoints).

elements.quote: PoCUS can answer a broad spectrum of remaining diagnostic questions and may also help to optimize and personalize therapy.
elements.reason: Briefly describes the proposed mechanism of action (answering diagnostic questions -> optimizing therapy).
No logic model is presented or described in the manuscript to show hypothesised relationships between intervention components and outcomes.

elements.quote: our main objective, as a new insight to this field, was to investigate how PoCUS improves clinical endpoints in patients with acute onset dyspnea.
elements.reason: The Introduction section explicitly states the main objective of the review.

elements.quote: The selected studies had to match our previously defined PICO (Patients, Intervention, Control, Outcome) framework: P: Adults and children... I: The examined intervention was PoCUS use... C: Control group included conventional diagnostic methods... O: For the primary outcomes, we defined time to diagnosis...
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states the use of the PICO framework to define the planned comparisons (Patients, Intervention, Control, Outcome).

elements.quote: Only randomized controlled trials (RCTs), and prospective and retrospective cohort studies were eligible for inclusion.
elements.reason: Eligible study designs are explicitly specified in the Selection Process section.

elements.quote: The Cochrane Library, MEDLINE, EMBASE and reference lists were searched to identify eligible trials (inception to October 14, 2021). There were no language restrictions.
elements.reason: Dissemination year (inception to Oct 14, 2021) and language (no restrictions) criteria are specified in the Abstract.
No evidence found distinguishing exclusion based on whether outcomes were not measured versus whether outcome results were not reported.

elements.quote: The selected studies had to match our previously defined PICO (Patients, Intervention, Control, Outcome) framework... I: The examined intervention was PoCUS use... C: Control group included conventional diagnostic methods...
elements.reason: Groups used in synthesis (PoCUS vs Control) are specified and linked to the PICO framework defined in the Methods.
While eligibility restrictions are listed (e.g., study design), no rationales are provided for why these specific restrictions were chosen.

elements.quote: We systematically searched MEDLINE (via PubMed), EMBASE, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) for eligible articles on 14 October, 2021.
elements.reason: The document explicitly states the search date (14 October, 2021) for the main databases.

elements.quote: We systematically searched MEDLINE (via PubMed), EMBASE, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) for eligible articles on 14 October, 2021.
elements.reason: Database names and coverage dates (inception to Oct 14, 2021 per text_2) are reported, but search interface/platform is only specified for MEDLINE (via PubMed), not for EMBASE or CENTRAL.

elements.quote: The protocol was prospectively registered via the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO)
elements.reason: No study register (e.g., ClinicalTrials.gov) was searched; PROSPERO was used for protocol registration only.

elements.quote: We also scanned the reference lists of included studies and the cited articles in Google Scholar.
elements.reason: The search engine name (Google Scholar) is reported, but the URL is not provided.

elements.quote: N/A
elements.reason: No organisations or manufacturers were contacted to identify studies.

elements.reason: No individuals were contacted to identify studies.

elements.quote: N/A
elements.reason: No specific journals or conference proceedings were consulted directly.

elements.quote: The detailed search key is outlined in the Additional Methods section.
elements.reason: The text refers to an 'Additional Methods section' for the detailed search key, but this section is not provided in the retrieved evidence. The provided images are forest plots and tables, not search strategies.

elements.quote: We applied 'title, abstract, author, keyword' filters in EMBASE-no other filters were used. We did not use any restrictions or limitations based on language or publication date.
elements.reason: Search limits (filters and lack of language/date restrictions) are described, but explicit justification referencing eligibility criteria for these specific limits is not provided in the text.

elements.quote: We report our results following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) recommendations [26].
elements.reason: The text cites PRISMA for reporting recommendations, but does not cite any published search approaches or filters used to construct the search strategy.
No mention of natural-language processing or text-analysis tools in the retrieved evidence.
No mention of tools used to translate search strings between sources in the retrieved evidence.
No mention of validation of the search strategy in the retrieved evidence.
No mention of peer review of the search strategy (e.g., PRESS) in the retrieved evidence.
The review focuses on PoCUS for dyspnea, implying a standard PICO structure. There is no evidence suggesting a non-PICO search structure was used.

elements.quote: two review authors (G.S. and C.S.) independently screened titles, abstracts, and then the full texts
elements.reason: The text explicitly states that two review authors screened titles, abstracts, and full texts.

elements.quote: two review authors (G.S. and C.S.) independently screened titles, abstracts, and then the full texts
elements.reason: The text explicitly states that the review authors 'independently screened' the records.

elements.quote: Discrepancies were resolved by two other review authors (Z.M. and M.R.).
elements.reason: The text describes the process for resolving discrepancies involving two other authors.
There is no description of processes used to obtain or confirm eligibility information from study investigators.
While no language restrictions were used, there is no report of methods used to translate abstracts or full articles.

elements.quote: removal of duplicates using a reference management software (EndNote X9, Clarivate Analytics)
elements.reason: The text describes the use of EndNote software for duplicate removal as part of the selection process.
No externally derived classifiers are identified or described.
No internally derived classifiers are identified or described.
No machine-learning prioritisation tools or screening stopping rules are described.
No crowdsourcing platforms are described.
No previously screened datasets used to eliminate records are described.

elements.quote: Data on the first author, publication year, countries, study design, number of patients in each group and their baseline characteristics (including age and gender), type of PoCUS protocol, examiners' practice and the available primary and secondary outcome parameters were extracted by two independent review authors (G.S. and C.S.)
elements.reason: The text explicitly states that data were extracted by two independent review authors.

elements.quote: extracted by two independent review authors (G.S. and C.S.)
elements.reason: The text explicitly states that the review authors worked independently.

elements.quote: Discrepancies were resolved by two other review authors (Z.M. and M.R.).
elements.reason: The text describes the process for resolving discrepancies between data collectors.

elements.quote: In the case of one study (Blans [46]), the author kindly provided the original data on patients with dyspnea, excluding all other causes.
elements.reason: The text describes a process where data was obtained directly from a study investigator.

elements.quote: using our standardized data collection form in Microsoft Excel.
elements.reason: The text specifies the software (Microsoft Excel) used for data collection.
The text states no language restrictions were used, but does not report methods for translating articles if non-English studies were included.
The text mentions extracting data from figures was difficult, but does not specify the software used for this extraction.
The text states there were no overlapping populations or duplicate data, but does not describe the decision rules for selecting data from multiple reports.

elements.quote: Data on the first author, publication year, countries, study design, number of patients in each group and their baseline characteristics (including age and gender), type of PoCUS protocol, examiners' practice and the available primary and secondary outcome parameters were extracted
elements.reason: Outcomes are referred to as 'available primary and secondary outcome parameters' in Methods (text_5) rather than explicitly listed and defined; specific outcomes appear in Results/Analysis sections (text_8, text_9) but definitions are limited.

elements.quote: We found no significant effects on 30-day re-admission rate... 30-day mortality... Time to diagnosis was the most cited endpoint... (MD - 63 min)
elements.reason: Time frames are specified for some outcomes (e.g., '30-day'), but others like 'Time to diagnosis' lack explicit measurement windows beyond units (minutes).
Text_5 states 'available primary and secondary outcome parameters were extracted' but does not explicitly state whether all compatible results within each outcome domain were sought.
As the statement regarding seeking all compatible results (e3) is missing, the process for selecting results when not all were sought is also not described.

elements.quote: There was no deviation from the protocol.
elements.reason: Explicitly reports that there were no deviations from the protocol, satisfying the requirement to report on changes to outcome domains.

elements.quote: There was no deviation from the protocol.
elements.reason: Explicitly reports that there were no deviations from the protocol, satisfying the requirement to report on changes to selection processes.
While 'Time to diagnosis' is noted as the 'most cited endpoint' (text_8), there is no explicit report of outcomes prioritized for interpreting conclusions with a rationale for that prioritization.

elements.quote: Data on the first author, publication year, countries, study design, number of patients in each group and their baseline characteristics (including age and gender), type of PoCUS protocol, examiners' practice and the available primary and secondary outcome parameters were extracted by two independent review authors
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly lists the variables sought for data extraction, including author details, study characteristics, patient demographics, and outcome parameters.

elements.quote: If the mean and SD were not reported in the article, we estimated them from the medians, quartiles, minimum and maximums using the Luo [32] and Shi [33] methods.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the assumption and method used to handle missing statistical data (estimating mean and SD from other statistics).

elements.quote: Based on the consensus of methodological and clinical experts, we created a standardized data collection sheet.
elements.reason: The authors created their own data collection sheet based on expert consensus rather than using a pre-existing external tool that would require citation.

elements.quote: For RCTs the RoB 2 tool (revised tool for Risk of Bias in randomized trials) was used, whereas for the cohorts, we used the ROBINS-I tool (Risk Of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Interventions) [27, 28].
elements.reason: The specific risk-of-bias tools (RoB 2 and ROBINS-I) are explicitly named in the text.
The text refers to Additional Tables for detailed descriptions but does not list the specific domains or items assessed in the provided text.

elements.quote: Based on the Cochrane proposal, the risk of bias assessment showed serious concern for only one article [48] and moderate (some concern in cases of RCTs) or low risk for all others.
elements.reason: Overall risk-of-bias judgements are reported (serious, moderate, low), but the specific rules used to derive these judgements are not explicitly detailed in the text.
No mention of adaptations made to the risk-of-bias tools in the provided text.
Standard tools (RoB 2, ROBINS-I) were used; no new tool was developed.

elements.quote: Two independent review authors (G.S. and C.S.) did the assessment, and an independent third investigator resolved any disagreements (F.D.).
elements.reason: The number of reviewers (two), their independence, and the disagreement-resolution procedure (third investigator) are clearly stated.
No description of processes used to obtain or confirm risk-of-bias information from study investigators.
No mention of automation tools used for risk-of-bias assessment.

elements.quote: For continuous outcomes, pooled mean differences (MDs), and for dichotomous variables, pooled odds ratios (ORs) along with their 95% confidence interval (CI), were calculated to investigate the differences between the compared arms.
elements.reason: The text explicitly specifies the effect measures used for continuous outcomes (mean differences) and dichotomous variables (odds ratios) in the Statistical Analysis section.
No thresholds or ranges for interpreting the magnitude of effect sizes (e.g., clinically significant mean difference) are reported in the provided text.

The text describes estimating mean and SD from other statistics for data extraction, but does not describe methods for re-expressing synthesized results using another effect measure (e.g., converting OR to RR).
While the effect measures are specified, the text does not provide a justification for why these specific measures (MD, OR) were chosen over alternatives.

elements.quote: The selected studies had to match our previously defined PICO (Patients, Intervention, Control, Outcome) framework: The risk of bias was assessed based on the recommendations of the Cochrane Collaboration. Two independent review authors (G.S. and C.S.) did the assessment, and an independent third investigator resolved any disagreements (F.D.). For RCTs the RoB 2 tool (revised tool for Risk of Bias in randomized trials) was used, whereas for the cohorts, we used the ROBINS-I tool (Risk Of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Interventions) [27, 28]. P: Adults and children who were admitted to the ED or to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU), or to another inpatient setting because of acute onset or worsening dyspnea were eligible. We also included studies enrolling patients who developed shortness of breath from unknown etiologies and were already hospitalized. Studies reporting on trauma-induced acute onset dyspnea, or pregnancy were excluded. Publication bias was assessed by visual inspection of the Funnel plots and the leave-one-out sensitivity analyses (see Additional Figs. 2 and 3). I: The examined intervention was PoCUS use on its own or in combination with conventional diagnostic measures. If PoCUS was applied in combination with conventional methods, the endpoints in each case should be able to be evaluated separately from the control arm.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the PICO framework used to determine study eligibility for the synthesis and specifies conditions for evaluating intervention endpoints, which constitutes the process for deciding eligibility.

elements.quote: If the mean and SD were not reported in the article, we estimated them from the medians, quartiles, minimum and maximums using the Luo [32] and Shi [33] methods.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly describes the method used to handle missing summary statistics (estimating mean and standard deviation from medians, quartiles, etc.) for the purpose of data synthesis in the meta-analysis.

elements.quote: The characteristics of the studies included in our systematic review and metaanalysis are presented in Table 1.
elements.reason: The text explicitly states that study characteristics are presented in Table 1, and Additional Tables are used for risk of bias and GRADE assessment (text_11), describing the tabular structures and data included.

elements.quote: If there were at least three studies for an outcome, a metaanalysis was performed, and the results displayed in forest plots.
elements.reason: The text explicitly describes the use of forest plots for displaying meta-analysis results and funnel plots for publication bias (text_11).
No explicit statement describing the basis for ordering or grouping studies within the tables or graphs (e.g., by year, sample size, or outcome) was found in the provided text.
Only standard graphical methods (forest plots, funnel plots) were reported; no non-standard graphs were used, so no rationale is required.

elements.quote: Our results are in contrast with a recently published guideline [61], which states that clinicians may use PoCUS in addition to the standard diagnostic pathway when there is diagnostic uncertainty. Based on our results, we recommend that all patients suffering from acute onset dyspnea should be managed by PoCUS as a standard and not only as a supplementary tool when standard diagnostic measures fail. ... Alrajab et al. [19] reported in a meta-analysis that the PoCUS group needed a significantly shorter time to show the presence or absence of pneumothorax. Their results are in line with our findings that PoCUS use can reduce time to diagnosis by more than one hour.
elements.reason: The authors explicitly interpret their results by contrasting them with a recently published guideline and comparing them to findings from a meta-analysis by Alrajab et al., thereby providing a general interpretation of the results in the context of other relevant evidence within the Discussion section.

elements.quote: Our study also has certain limitations. There was substantial heterogeneity regarding the age groups as we included infants and patients older than 59 years [40, 47]. Severity of illness, as indicated by the patients' different medical conditions, also showed heterogeneity as some articles included intubated, mechanically ventilated patients, while others excluded this group [41, 47]. Furthermore, not all patients had dyspnea only as the sole complaint. Some articles also included patients with coughing or chest pain, which further increased the heterogeneity of the study population (Table 1). ... The diversity of PoCUS protocols may be another important factor behind the high heterogeneity of the results and this is a key point and limitation at the same time, from both the methodological and clinical points of view.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly identifies and discusses limitations of the included evidence, citing heterogeneity in age, severity, and PoCUS protocols.

elements.quote: Our study also has certain limitations. There was substantial heterogeneity regarding the age groups as we included infants and patients older than 59 years [40, 47]. elements.quote: diversity of PoCUS protocols may be another important factor behind the high heterogeneity of the results... extracting numerical data from figures was particularly difficult... elements.reason: The text discusses the potential impact of the limitations, linking protocol diversity to 'high heterogeneity of the results', noting data extraction 'difficulty', and concluding that limitations highlight the 'need for the development of gold standards'.

elements.quote: The results of this systematic review and meta-analysis indicate that all patients admitted with acute onset dyspnea should be examined with PoCUS to reduce time to diagnosis, time to treatment, LOS and potentially mortality.
elements.reason: The text explicitly states recommendations for clinical practice regarding the use of PoCUS for patients with acute onset dyspnea.
